prompt.context_jp: ⟨根底から揺るがす女___現れた⟩
prompt.prompt_jp: 根底から揺るがす女___現れた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that introduces this woman as new information.

feedback.correct_en: The woman is being introduced for the first time as a dramatic new element; が marks this new-information subject in an existential/appearance clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose she is already known to the listener, which contradicts the 'appeared' narrative beat.

contrast_examples.en: The woman (we were discussing) did show up.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家___いつもの無表情のまま、年配の男性客に小さく頭を下げている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 三軒家___いつもの無表情のまま、頭を下げている。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for the already-known protagonist being described?

feedback.correct_en: Sangenya is a known character; は marks her as the topic whose action is being narrated in a descriptive beat.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would frame her as newly spotted information, inappropriate when the camera is simply continuing to describe her.

contrast_examples.jp: 三軒家は頭を下げている。
三軒家が頭を下げている。

prompt.context_jp: その足立の目___、客の顔を見るが早いか、驚きに見開かれた。
prompt.prompt_jp: その足立の目___、驚きに見開かれた。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle marking the subject in this sudden-event clause.

feedback.correct_en: This is a narrated moment of sudden perception; が marks the subject of the eye-opening event as new, focused information.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'Adachi's eyes' a general topic, losing the vivid 'as soon as he saw...' punch.

prompt.context_jp: 「“僕のお客” 誰___決めたの？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 誰___決めたの？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits a question demanding to identify 'who exactly'?

feedback.correct_en: With interrogatives like 誰, が is required to ask for identification — 'who was the one who decided'. This is the exhaustive-listing/identification が.
feedback.incorrect_en: 誰は決めたの is ungrammatical; は cannot attach to an unknown wh-subject in this type of question.

prompt.context_jp: 「私に売れない家___ありません！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私に売れない家___ありません。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits Sangenya's signature line?

feedback.correct_en: は here carries contrastive/categorical negation: 'as for houses I can't sell — there are none'. It sets up the whole category and denies it.
feedback.incorrect_en: 家がありません would just mean 'there is no house', missing the emphatic 'no such house exists' flavor that defines her tagline.

contrast_examples.en: There is no house (of the kind) I can't sell.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家が来てからというもの、足立の成績___かつての勢いを失い、今は低迷していると陰でささやかれていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 足立の成績___かつての勢いを失い…
prompt.prompt_en: Topic marker for 'as for Adachi's performance'?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence is a general commentary about Adachi's performance as a known topic; は frames it and the predicate elaborates.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would create a focus/exhaustive reading ('it is Adachi's performance that...') which doesn't match the explanatory tone.

prompt.context_jp: 足立は自分の席にも向かわず、フロアの真ん中___拳を固く握りしめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: フロアの真ん中___拳を握りしめていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the location of the action?

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location where a dynamic action (clenching fists) takes place.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a static existence point or destination, not the site of an ongoing action.

prompt.context_jp: 応接室のソファに腰を下ろしたの___、きちんとしたスーツに身を包んだ中年の男だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ソファに腰を下ろしたの___、中年の男だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this 'the one who X was Y' identification sentence?

feedback.correct_en: The nominalized clause 'the one who sat down' is the topic, and the predicate identifies what/who it was; は is standard for this presentational pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly re-focus the already-foregrounded clause; the natural pattern here is Xのは〜だ.

contrast_examples.en: The one who came was a man.

prompt.context_jp: 「今夜___先約があります」
prompt.prompt_jp: 今夜___先約があります。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits here, implying 'tonight (as opposed to other nights)'?

feedback.correct_en: は on 今夜 gives a contrastive 'tonight specifically', politely implying another night might be possible — exactly Adachi's deflection.
feedback.incorrect_en: 今夜が would exhaustively assert 'it's tonight that...', odd here; に alone with ある is possible but loses the polite brush-off nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 「事故物件」という言葉が出たとたん、営業フロアの空気___目に見えて冷え込んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: フロアの空気___目に見えて冷え込んだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the change-of-state subject here?

feedback.correct_en: This is a sudden observable change tied to the moment the word was spoken; が marks the subject of this event clause, keeping the focus on what visibly happened.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn it into a general statement about the atmosphere, losing the dramatic 'the moment X, Y happened' structure.

prompt.context_jp: 「この物件 私___売ります」
prompt.prompt_jp: この物件 私___売ります。
prompt.prompt_en: Sangenya is volunteering. Which particle marks 'I' as the one who will sell it?

feedback.correct_en: She is identifying herself as THE one (among all who refused) to take on the property — classic exhaustive-listing が ('I'm the one who will sell it').
feedback.incorrect_en: 私は売ります would just state her intention as topic, losing the 'it'll be me, specifically' challenge to the room.

contrast_examples.en: I (am the one who) will sell it.

prompt.context_jp: 「私の彼 奥さん___いるんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私の彼、奥さん___いるんです。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'has a wife' in this confession?

feedback.correct_en: With いる/ある for possession/existence, the possessed noun takes が: 奥さんがいる = 'he has a wife'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 奥さんは would make 'the wife' a known topic, which doesn't fit this reveal; を is wrong because いる is intransitive.

contrast_examples.en: (As for a wife,) he doesn't have one.

prompt.context_jp: 窓の外___は、風が少しずつ強まり始めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 窓の外___、風が少しずつ強まり始めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the location where the wind was picking up?

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location of a dynamic event — the wind strengthening — happening outside the window.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark static existence; を marks a path, neither fits this scenic description of ongoing weather.

prompt.context_jp: 「お隣さん___イヤでも チェンジできないわけなんだから」
prompt.prompt_jp: お隣さん___イヤでも、チェンジできない。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle gives the contrastive 'even if (the neighbor) is unpleasant' nuance?

feedback.correct_en: は inside the でも-clause gives a contrastive 'even in the case that the neighbor is unpleasant', setting up the inability to change them.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would focus on identifying the subject as new info, but here the speaker is contrasting a hypothetical case — は fits.

contrast_examples.jp: 隣人はイヤでも我慢する。
contrast_examples.en: Even if the neighbor is unpleasant, I endure.

prompt.context_jp: 三軒家が来てから、営業所の中___はいくつもの目に見えない線が引かれるようになっていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 営業所の中___目に見えない線が引かれていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks where the lines came to exist?

feedback.correct_en: The passive 線が引かれる focuses on the resulting location of the lines; に marks the place where they come to exist.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the site of the drawing action, but here the focus is on the lines' resulting presence, not the drawers' activity.

contrast_examples.jp: 地図に線が引かれている。
contrast_examples.en: Lines are drawn on the map.

prompt.context_jp: 「僕___対応してる僕の客ですよ！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 僕___対応してる僕の客ですよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Adachi is insisting it's HE who has been handling the client. Which particle?

feedback.correct_en: Inside the relative clause 僕が対応してる ('whom I am handling'), が marks the subject — relative clauses typically take が, not は.
feedback.incorrect_en: は generally cannot appear as the subject of a relative/noun-modifying clause; 僕は対応してる客 sounds broken.

prompt.context_jp: 「___ 申します 足立聡さん ライフ・プレジデント生命で働きませんか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: ___申します、足立聡さん。
prompt.prompt_en: Which set phrase means 'to put it bluntly / to get straight to the point'?

feedback.correct_en: 単刀直入に申します = 'I'll come straight to the point', the standard polite preface for a frank proposal.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一刀両断 means 'cutting decisively (through indecision)' and 二束三文 means 'dirt cheap' — neither prefaces a direct statement.

prompt.context_jp: その落ち着き払った態度が、かえって足立の胸の奥の火に___を注いだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 火に___を注いだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes this idiom meaning 'added fuel to the fire'?

feedback.correct_en: 火に油を注ぐ is the fixed idiom meaning to make a bad situation worse — exactly what Sangenya's calm did to Adachi.
feedback.incorrect_en: 水を注ぐ would extinguish the fire (opposite meaning); 塩 fits no comparable idiom here.

contrast_examples.en: To add fuel to the fire.
To throw cold water on (a mood).

prompt.context_jp: 「私のこと ___まで好きだって 言ってますから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私のこと、___まで好きだと言ってます。
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrase means 'to the very core / through and through'?

feedback.correct_en: 骨の髄まで好き ('loves me to the marrow') is the fixed intensifier Murota uses — it emphasizes total, bone-deep devotion.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心の底から好き is natural but doesn't take まで the same way; 腹の底 collocates with 'laughing' or 'hidden feelings', not love.

contrast_examples.en: To love from the bottom of one's heart.

prompt.context_jp: 家を探しに来た客のものとは違う、___するような鋭さがあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___するような鋭さがあった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb describes 'appraising/sizing someone up'?

feedback.correct_en: 値踏みする = 'to size up / appraise someone's worth', fitting Gomi's evaluative gaze.
feedback.incorrect_en: 値下げ (price reduction) and 値引き (discount) describe lowering a price, not evaluating a person.

contrast_examples.en: To size the other person up.

prompt.context_jp: 「3ヶ月も___ 足立聡 あなたが___お客が 私のまいたチラシに食い付いた」
prompt.prompt_jp: 3ヶ月も___おいて…
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb means 'to leave alone / neglect'?

feedback.correct_en: 放っておく = 'to leave alone, neglect'. Sangenya's point: you neglected the client for three months.
feedback.incorrect_en: 払う means 'pay/brush off' and 振る means 'wave/reject' — neither fits '(leave) untended for 3 months'.

prompt.context_jp: 心理的___物件とは、過去に自殺や殺人などがあり、買い手が心理的な抵抗を感じる物件のことである。
prompt.prompt_jp: 心理的___物件
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes the real estate term for a 'stigmatized property'?

feedback.correct_en: 心理的瑕疵物件 is the industry term — 瑕疵 (defect/flaw) is the specific legal word for property defects.
feedback.incorrect_en: 過失 means 'negligence' (a legal fault by a person); 欠乏 means 'shortage/deficiency' of a substance. Neither names property defects.

prompt.context_jp: 今夜ばかりは、___験は何でも担ぎたい気分だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___験は何でも担ぎたい。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb collocates with 験 to mean 'rely on any good-luck charm/omen'?

feedback.correct_en: 験を担ぐ is the set phrase for 'to be superstitious / rely on omens' — here in potential form 担げる.
feedback.incorrect_en: 持つ or 取る don't collocate with 験 in this idiomatic meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 「どういう方なら ___んでしょうか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: どういう方なら___んでしょうか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which word is the polite equivalent of いい in a question to a client?

feedback.correct_en: よろしい is the polite/formal counterpart of いい, standard when confirming a client's preferences.
feedback.incorrect_en: かわいい and うれしい are feelings/descriptions, not polite acceptability markers.

contrast_examples.jp: これでよろしいでしょうか。

prompt.context_jp: Adachi confronts Sangenya about his stolen client.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural for Adachi's accusation 'Mr. Shigeno is MY client'?

choices.text: 茂野様は 僕のお客です。
茂野様が 僕のお客です。

feedback.correct_en: With 茂野様 already in the conversation, は marks him as the topic and 僕のお客 as the predicate ('as for Shigeno, he's my client').
feedback.incorrect_en: 茂野様が僕のお客です would strangely identify Shigeno as 'the one who is my client' — awkward since Shigeno isn't being contrasted with other candidates.

contrast_examples.en: That (specific) person is my client (not that one).

prompt.context_jp: Kokoro reflects on love and the women involved with Miyazawa.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'there is no right form of love'?

choices.text: 愛に正しい形なんてない。
愛で正しい形なんてない。
愛が正しい形なんてない。

feedback.correct_en: 愛に正しい形はない uses に to mark the domain ('in love, there is no...'), the natural existential pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark means/location of an action; が would make 愛 the subject, which doesn't fit the 'X にはYがない' idiom.

contrast_examples.en: There is no right answer in life.

contrast_examples.jp: 仕事に失敗はつきもの。

prompt.context_jp: Shigeno happily tells Adachi that Sangenya found him a great apartment.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version matches Shigeno's warm, casual report?

choices.text: 三軒家さんが いいマンション 見つけてくれたよ。
三軒家さんは いいマンション 見つけてくれたよ。

feedback.correct_en: が is natural here: Shigeno is reporting fresh, newsworthy information about who did him a favor — 'Sangenya found me...'. The favor-giver as new info takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would frame Sangenya as the established topic and compare her to someone else, which doesn't fit this cheerful announcement.

prompt.context_jp: Adachi's self-description to colleagues.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing matches Adachi's casual, self-deprecating line?

choices.text: 僕は心優しき王子様じゃないから。
僕が心優しき王子様じゃないから。

feedback.correct_en: 僕は... is natural self-topicalization: 'as for me, I'm not a kind prince'. This is a general statement about himself.
feedback.incorrect_en: 僕が would exhaustively identify 'I am the one who is not the kind prince', an odd focus that doesn't fit a general self-description.

contrast_examples.jp: 僕はそんな人間じゃない。
contrast_examples.en: I'm not that kind of person.
It was me who did it.
